title: LOD generation breaks basic armature weights setup
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7640) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600H with Radeon Graphics (12 threads)

### Issue description

An incredibly simple, extremely basic armature setup doesn't work in Godot.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/febd3c7c-1bb6-461a-9ed4-2aea918d7294

Incredulous, I imported the same .glb file into both Unity and Unreal. This was so utterly basic surely I was maybe just missing a step or something. But no, as expected, the .glb file works as you'd expect in both Unity and Unreal.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a cube in Blender.
Subdivide.
Create armature.
Parent armature to cube with automatic weights.
Play around with armature a bit in pose mode to make sure everything's working right.
Export to .glb.
Import .glb into Godot.
Play around with skeleton in Godot.
Try your best to contain bewilderment and despair.

Bonus task: import same .glb into Unity and Unreal, just to confirm you're not going crazy.
Notice that skeleton works as expected in Unity and Unreal.
Try your best to contain bewilderment and despair.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[basic_skeleton.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20208230/basic_skeleton.zip)
